uncertainty: Culture-curious SSE commuters repeatedly lack a convenient way to discover Riga culture and would choose ninety-second audio over the original listing.
Some repeat listeners might eventually pay for a subscription; no supplied receipt supports their willingness to pay or a price.
Cultural venues might sponsor relevant stories to reach prospective visitors. The museum invitation is a public programming signal, not evidence of a sponsorship budget or purchase intent.

Proposed test, not run: invite ten consenting SSE commuters, offer three manually checked episodes alongside their source listings, and ask which format they prefer and why. Keep the €20 budget; pass the initial repeat-use screen only if four voluntarily play a different episode without individual r
No customer contact, listening tests, repeat plays or payment evidence exists.
dissent: A dated museum lecture supports editorial feasibility more directly than customer demand; EU tourism totals are even further removed from student commuting.
Free listings may already solve discovery better than audio, especially when listeners need dates and location details.
Four repeats among ten recruited students could reflect novelty or politeness. A free cultural experiment can still be worthwhile, but that threshold cannot establish a sustainable business.
